title: Grateful Dead Live at Worcester Polytechnic Institute on 1970-05-09
lineage: SBD > MR > ? > DAT > CDR > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Muddy, hissy portable‑cassette capture of a short 1970 acoustic set – Jerry’s folk vocals shine while the recording struggles.
ai_review.review: The tape offers only a brief acoustic portion of a spring‑1970 show, highlighted by Jerry Garcia’s clear, folk‑style singing and Pigpen’s harmonica work on songs like “Deep Ellum Blues” and “Black Peter.”  Technically the source is an audience/portable‑cassette recording that is saturated, hissy and overloaded during the electric set, making it difficult to enjoy despite the historical value.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers agree the performance (especially the acoustic set) is decent, but the recording quality is consistently described as poor; the weighted average of show (≈3) and recording (≈2) yields a mid‑range rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Hissy, saturated and muddy sound; audible overload on the electric portion; short duration; likely recorded with a portable cassette microphone rather than a true soundboard feed.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A brief, intimate acoustic set that showcases Jerry and Pigpen; the electric second half is either missing or badly captured, leaving the tape feeling incomplete.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for a strong, clear folk‑style vocal and acoustic guitar work; occasional steel guitar noted.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s harmonica highlighted; organ briefly joins on “Black Peter.”
